source: Follow-up to the independent review's same-turn affected-hit finding.
problem: After selecting a later state-affected hit, the matcher still applies that branch-local legal-roll set to every roll-scaled component in the branch. In a two-hit turn such as Aurora Beam -> Attack drop -> Tackle, the prefix snapshot is valid only for the later Tackle against p1; using it for the earlier Aurora Beam against p2 can accept the earlier component against the wrong state.
required_mechanism: Return the protocol target side together with the branch-local legal-roll set.
Use branch-local support only for the selected affected target side.
Retain the existing boundary pre-state support for all other components in that branch.
regression_prediction: For Aurora Beam damage to p2 followed by a nonzero p2 Attack drop and p2 Tackle damage to p1, the reconstructed support must be labeled p1 and must not replace p2's pre-state support.
containment: Do not widen action attribution, roll ranges, residual handling, or divergence classes.
Do not change the Rust prefix snapshot mechanism.
Do not reinterpret retained-row engine divergences as matches.
